title: Choose Bidd's visual world
question: The roll landed on the Sheet Banner. Keep it, take the Bid Card, go with the category standard, or re-roll.

options.label: The Sheet Banner
options.lineage: Hand-painted bedsheet banners hung on chapter houses for Bid Day and gameday
options.thesis: Every closet is a banner a chapter painted itself: black outlines on a white sheet, with the campus color filled in by hand.
options.viewport: One sheet hung edge to edge from rope ties. BIDD is painted huge in black outline with a crimson fill, 'Be 1 of 1.' is brushed below, and a campus switch repaints every fill.
options.risk: Handmade can slide into clip-art or amateur. It needs disciplined block letters and a strict grid, never loose brushwork.

raised.raise: One pull, whole sheet: switching campus repaints every fill in a single propagated motion. The tenant swap is the signature interaction.
The sheet's storage creases become a strict panel grid that every block snaps to, and small screens scale the banner rather than re-flow it.
Closet Cup standings are painted as bold tally bars, an argument rather than a table.
Every listing and drop carries its Greek-calendar moment and season day (Fall Cup · Day 23).
Bidd's black frame never moves. Only the campus-filled window inside it changes.
One shared clock: drop countdowns and the Cup season run on the same visible timer, and what's next is announced before it opens.

options.label: The Bid Card
options.lineage: Bid Day bid cards: the sealed envelope every new member opens and runs home with
options.thesis: Every drop is a sealed bid: black-and-white card stock on the outside, your campus color waiting inside.
options.viewport: A half-open envelope fills the viewport. The card sliding out reads BIDD / Be 1 of 1. over a crimson liner, with the access-code field printed on the card itself.
options.risk: It's the literal reading of the name and where most runs would land. It can also drift toward wedding stationery and cold luxury.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Bidd as a broadcast index of numbered pages.
options.viewport: P100: Closet Cup scores built from blocks.
options.case: Loses both axes: the Cup works as a scores page, but SEC students have never seen teletext.
options.kept: A strict cell grid that small screens scale rather than re-flow.
options.risk: Retro novelty with no campus roots.

options.label: Du Bois Data Portraits
options.thesis: Pitch statistics as hand-inked graphic arguments.
options.viewport: A spiral of chapter sales coiling around the hook number.
options.case: Loses both axes: it makes the numbers land, but the closet isn't a chart, and borrowing Du Bois's portraits of Black American life for an SEC Greek marketplace risks reading as tone-deaf.
options.kept: Data as bold argument: Cup standings get invented, painted forms, never a default table.
options.risk: A cultural misfit for this audience.

options.label: Miura-Fold Sheet
options.thesis: The closet as a sheet that unfolds from a packet in one pull.
options.viewport: A packet that unfolds into the closet.
options.case: Loses both axes: students don't identify with aerospace origami, and folding doesn't explain closets or drops.
options.kept: One pull deploys the whole sheet: a campus switch repaints every fill at once.
options.risk: Reads as an engineering demo, not campus life.

options.label: Pickling Brine Calendar
options.thesis: The Greek calendar as a shelf of maturing jars.
options.viewport: A seasonal shelf with one jar per calendar moment.
options.case: Loses both axes: jars and brine have nothing to do with campus fashion, though the seasonal calendar does map to the Greek one.
options.kept: Every item carries its season stamp and day count.
options.risk: A cute food metaphor that muddies the offer.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: Bidd as a rendered console around a small live window.
options.viewport: Embossed toggles around a postcard-size feed.
options.case: Loses both axes: beveled 90s chrome reads as a novelty and fights the black-and-white pin.
options.kept: A fixed frame around a live window: Bidd's frame holds still and only the campus window changes.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: Drops performed as live code on a club floor.
options.viewport: A code buffer where the cursor line is the next drop.
options.case: Loses both axes: live-coding culture is foreign to the audience and hides the marketplace.
options.kept: One shared clock, with the next change announced before it lands.
options.risk: A hacker costume that alienates the audience.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean resale marketplace in black and white with a campus-color accent, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Wordmark nav, a search bar, moment-tag chips and a two-up listing grid, Depop-style.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Depop and Curtsy by design.
